newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon army chief says army not in politics.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon army chief says army not in politics.

text.p: Lebanon's army commander General Emile Lahoud said on Wednesday the army was loyal to the country's political leaders and did not engage in politics.

Lahoud's rare public statement appeared to be a reply to Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, who last week charged that an unnamed intelligence agency was failing to obey political directives and was threatening civilian rule.
Some newspapers and television stations said at the time Hariri was referring to the army, but this has not been officially confirmed.

"The army has always maintained its obedience to the decisions of the political leadership decisions, which means cabinet decisions, and has refused the logic of political bias in its ranks," Lahoud said in a directive to the 63,000-strong army.
"The army is not in a position of political competition with any body," he said.

"It is very well known in the country who works on destroying the civilian institutions, and neither the army nor its bodies has any relation with that issue," the directive added without elaborating.
Without naming Hariri, it said: "The army commander expresses regret at such a declaration by a high government official."
